clue.text: Relation with a bit of money entertaining you and me

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or host, so the coin holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a coin is a single piece of money
us is the pronoun covering you and me together

explanation.surface: A relative turns up with some loose change and treats the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: A first cousin is a family relative, the child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Designer Jean and I were first up in a state of ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the whole string is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Jean Muir was a British fashion designer
those who led were in front, coming first

explanation.surface: A fashion designer and the speaker were the earliest to be up, in a happy frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole string around. Jean Muir was a well-known London fashion designer; 'were first' is the past of lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirium can mean wild excitement or rapture as well as a feverish confusion.

clue.text: Where the roofer may be working for no money

definitions.text: Where the roofer may be working
definitions.meaning: taken literally, a roofer works up on top of a building
the idiom used of a drink or meal given free by the establishment

explanation.surface: A tradesman up on a roof doing a job unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means provided free by the bar or business; read literally it places someone atop a home.

clue.text: A cat's peculiar habits — they may be conveying a cry for help!

definitions.text: they may be conveying a cry for help!

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or out of the usual, so these letters come in a strange order

parts.note: ways are someone's customary habits

explanation.surface: A cat's odd behaviour is presented as a desperate plea for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peculiar' rearranges A CATS into CASTA. The definition pictures shipwrecked people sending an SOS, perhaps a message in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Marooned survivors on a desert island are the classic senders of a distress signal or bottled message.

clue.text: Feeble border penetrated by a thousand

indicators.note: penetrated says the first piece is pierced, with the second going inside it

parts.note: a lip is the rim or edge of something
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A weak frontier broken through by a thousand invaders.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means weak or lacking firmness, as in a limp excuse.

clue.text: Governor of bits round area to the north

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading upwards, backwards
round says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: parts are bits or pieces

explanation.surface: An official in charge of scraps of territory around an area further north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts A inside PARTS for PARATS, and 'to the north' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in the ancient Persian empire.

clue.text: He's a sore struggling swimmer

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man in pain is battling to stay afloat in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea creature that moves through water is a swimmer in the broad sense, a small upright fish.

clue.text: In sea with rickety canoe, one getting cold

indicators.note: a rickety thing is shaky and falling apart, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
C stands for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Out on the water in a flimsy boat, a lone paddler is getting chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic describes things found in or belonging to the open sea, an adjectival phrase swap.

clue.text: Gang somewhere in Cheshire finishing early

indicators.note: finishing early says the place loses its final letter

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in the English county of Cheshire

explanation.surface: A band of people in a Cheshire town calling it a day ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Crewe is a town in Cheshire, a county in north-west England; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working or hanging about together, like a gang.

clue.text: Italian in a crowd at match creates stir

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a gate is the attendance at a sporting fixture
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: An Italian fan among the spectators at a football game causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport the 'gate' is the number of spectators at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up or shake, whether a liquid or a crowd.

clue.text: Son least heavy, carrying least weight?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees
the lightest thing weighs the least

explanation.surface: A boy who is the lightest of the family, with the smallest load.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carrying least weight is the least important, a pun on influence and physical heaviness.

clue.text: Rod for fish

definitions.meaning: an old measure of length, five and a half yards, also called a pole
a freshwater fish with spiny fins

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old unit of length equal to a rod and a common freshwater fish.

clue.text: Beastly noise coming from gran, eighty

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An elderly grandmother making an odd sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's cry is a sound made by an animal, playing on beastly as both nasty and of beasts.

clue.text: Wife has jumper, something very large

parts.note: a hopper is anything that hops or jumps, like a grasshopper

explanation.surface: A wife owns a sweater that is enormous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is British for a sweater, but here it means something that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is informal for anything huge, including a big lie.

clue.text: Thinking too much of maiden maybe, sailor goes under

indicators.note: in a down clue, goes under places the sailor below the first piece

parts.note: a maiden is a cricket over in which no runs are scored
a rating is a non-commissioned sailor

explanation.surface: Overestimating a young woman, perhaps, as a seaman sinks.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over of six balls with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrate someone is to hold too high an opinion of them, to value them excessively.

clue.text: Is something soiled so inexpensive?

parts.note: something grubby or dirtied might sell cheaply, playing on the idiom for a bargain price

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether a stained item is reduced because it is dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally suggests dirt making goods cheap, while really meaning extremely cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means extraordinarily low-priced, and the clue reads it as cheap because grubby.

clue.text: I'm mingling with countrymen etc. in local meeting place

indicators.note: mingling means mixing together, so all these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone socialises with rural folk at the village hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbourhood hall used for gatherings and events serves residents of a district.

clue.text: Aromatic plant involved girl in expense

parts.note: cost is the expense of something
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fragrant herb dragged a young woman into spending money.
explanation.definitionFit: Costmary is a fragrant herb of the daisy family, once used to flavour ale.

clue.text: Merriest nuts in boats

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: The most cheerful crazy people out on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek and Roman warships with three banks of oars are vessels.

clue.text: 'Citizenship' at school maybe for UK citizen?

definitions.meaning: citizenship is one of the topics taught in British schools, an example of a field of study
a British national is a person owing allegiance to the Crown

explanation.surface: Is a school course in citizenship meant for British nationals?
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a classroom discipline and a person living under a monarch.

clue.text: Reward offered for ship commandeered by rebels

definitions.meaning: a payment offered for capturing someone
HMS ..., the Royal Navy ship seized in the famous 1789 mutiny

explanation.surface: A prize is put up for a vessel that mutineers have taken over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a reward offered for capture and the name of the ship famously taken in a mutiny.

clue.text: Makes a protest, there being barriers

definitions.meaning: to rail is to complain bitterly or rant
railings or fences along an edge

explanation.surface: A demonstrator objects when fences are put up.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to complain loudly; as a noun, the bars forming a fence.

clue.text: Nun entertained by monks is terrified

indicators.note: entertained by says the answer is held within the following words

explanation.surface: A nun put up by a group of monks is frightened.
explanation.definitionFit: A nun is addressed by the title of a female religious, a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Seaweed's flavour

definitions.meaning: with 's read as is: the word is a name for a kind of seaweed

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a coarse seaweed and a strong, sharp taste, with 's read as is.

clue.text: Must die?

definitions.meaning: mustiness, the fungal growth on damp things
a form or cast into which molten material is poured

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a fungus growth, also called must, and a shaping cast or die.

clue.text: Get rid of noise, internal ring

indicators.note: internal says the ring is placed inside the noise

parts.note: a din is a loud noise
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Eliminate the racket of a ring sounding inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to kill or dispose of someone, informally.

clue.text: Boy getting so cruel gets by

definitions.text: Boy getting so cruel gets by

parts.words: Boy getting so cruel gets by
parts.note: cruel is the plain sense; and if the word boy loses its centre letter, it becomes by

explanation.surface: A lad who becomes so unkind somehow muddles through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruel' is the plain definition. Read the answer as an instruction: BOY with its heart, the middle O, removed becomes BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartless means unfeeling and cruel; literally it also says lacking the central letter.

clue.text: Drink that's nastier when poured out

indicators.note: pouring out spills things everywhere, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A beverage that tastes worse once it leaves the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Italian port's birds, small number coming in

definitions.note: the possessive, belonging to the port, stands for the adjective of Genoa

indicators.note: coming in says the number goes inside the birds

parts.note: geese are large waterbirds
No is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A harbour town in Italy with flocks of birds and a few arrivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things from Genoa, the major port of north-west Italy.
